I cannot recommend this game cause it's too much based on RNG. The two easiest modes are pretty doable if your vocabulary isn't that of a toddler. From hard it gets HARD. Meaning you need good rolls on your perks or you're not gonna make it. Getting boards with 4xA, 4xO, 3xT, 3xE and a X and C isn't gonna give me a lot of options now, does it? Also, you can focus on extra points or being able to switch your letters into other letters, then a special round comes along where special tiles don't count. Have fun with your 5 accumulated gold tiles not doing ♥♥♥♥ the whole round. It's just too much RNG on several different fronts, instead of based on how many words you actually know. Oh, and just to make my point clear, I ended up using ChatGPT for 2 games straight to see if it was possible, and it's not. You can only win if the game gives you the tiles to make long words with, if it doesn't, you're screwed anyway.

Not there yet, unfortunately. Gets very frustrating when the game just FILLS your board with vowels... Puts you into a completely unwinnable situation and it happens very often. I've also found a lot of the upgrades to be very boring and unimaginative. Many don't feel good or useful and synergy so far has seemed extremely elusive to me. I don't think ten rounds is enough to really get a fun build going the vast majority of the time and I don't really find myself looking forward to the end of a round as a result, which is a huge problem for a game like this. These two issues combined just sap my will to play. At a minimum, there needs to be some kind of weighting system to the RNG to ensure that the player isn't completely inundated with vowels if they already have a bunch on the board. At least make it less likely than it is. I may come back to try again if this is fixed.

This game is insanely hard. I don't mean that the English language is hard, but the way the game presents modifiers, upgrades, and the overall score system is too harsh. Playing on hard mode, if you are 3 rounds into the run you can already be at the Reset/Lose scenario. It is almost impossible to build up a run late, and when you start losing, it's almost impossible to find a way out. The scaling doesn't make any sense, and outside beating A,B,C once, I am not sure I will continue to play. HUGE fan of GMTK, even participated in the last jam, however, this game isn't polished enough. Needs more modifiers, needs stronger upgrades, needs a way out when your run isn't going too well. The idea is good, execution is poor. I'm not saying "oh in balatro they do this, try to do that as well", I have played countless deck builders and rogue-likes. I just wish the Reset/Lose point would be further in the run, instead of having to reset on round 1-4 every time I don't get strong starting modifiers/upgrades.

Doesn't really have much staying power as a concept. The act of picking out high-scoring words takes long enough to kill any sense of momentum, and the power-ups feel like they're intentionally designed to almost never create runaway scaling situations, so it kinda just ends up feeling like Boggle with more steps and not much more payoff. It's probably frustrating to the dev to be compared unfavorably to Balatro, but Word Play has too much friction inherent to the design to get away with such uninteresting power-up combinations, and Balatro is the perfect case study in why you should make the opposite choice. I feel like I would need to sit through many more matches to find a truly good set of power-ups, whereas Balatro feels like a run can change dramatically with a single Joker, and that's the hook Word Play is missing for me right now.

This game lacks actual substance. It's fun for a bit if you like words, but drops off if you want anything more than words. The actual items and pickups all feel extremely low-impact. There are so many "upgrades" that say something like "Gives 1 bonus point every play, increases by 1 every time you use like 5 vowels in a single word" or something. There are other upgrades and builds that focus on different tile types (like you see in the exciting-looking title graphic), however these upgrades and tiles, even when built around, take nearly an entire game to see do ANYTHING, let alone anything major or impactful. It often goes "oh cool, I got a gold tile upgrade, yet after 10 rounds and like 30-40 words played, I've seen more than one gold tile in the same word maybe once? Twice?" It's just not interesting at all. This lackluster set of items forces you to continue using longer and longer words as you move up in difficulty. The items that are supposed to shape the run end up enforcing constraints, but even when I find myself playing to these constraints, I find myself bored of looking through my limited lexicon for any possible words I could play. Often, nothing comes to me (you try finding a word that has more vowels than consonants and ends in a "D" that is longer than 6 letters, with no "E" in it... Yeah, not so easy, oh and by the way if you can't find a word that fits that narrow intersection with the letters provided, you get next to no points for the word). This sort of thing would be fine if that were a one-off run, where other runs were spent dialing into builds and playing to the strengths of your letter bag or perks, but it's almost every single run where every reward screen you get 3 boring options which will do absolutely nothing to help you on the harder levels. The problem is that on a normal length run, you only get like 10-14 rewards screens. If you sell them, you get "refreshes," which barely help if you're going for any sort of letter-bag build (as you may end up refreshing away a key special letter). There's no counterplay for the limited rewards options. That is, I can't sell a perk for a different perk later on. Once I sell it, it's gone (into refreshes). Therefore, you either get extremely lucky with a good perk choice at some point in the run, or your run just grinds to a halt at the higher levels, with absolutely nothing you can do about it. Other roguelikes are fun, in my opinion, because the randomness throws you into a unique run every time. Issues that come up and screw your build can be played around, and you can always counterplay the randomness in some way. This game is not like that. If you strike out early, you'll almost certainly fail the run. And that's just not fun. This could be resolved by putting more diverse and powerful items into the game. More specialized, but more impactful. For example: one of the best items I've gotten was a "x2 word score for dot tiles, increases by 0.2 for every dot tile successfully played." -- insanely good if you're running dot tiles. However, for the rest of the entire run, I never got another dot tile related item. Just stupid bonus point items, or some variation of "replace 1 letter with a consonant" active item. If there were more of these specialized items, you'd have the ability to pair them together in interesting and unique ways, or if there were some way to obtain more chances at perks, or some way to pivot your build later on, there would be less of a chance you simply get unavoidably screwed on the later levels. If you're good at coming up with words, and you're looking for a game where you do nothing but come up with words given increasingly difficult constraints, this could be for you. Personally, though, I was hoping for that PLUS an interesting "build-driven" roguelike, and I unfortunately did not find that here.

I am pushing 50, so maybe this kind of game and my addiction to it actually shows that I am the gaming equivalent to a retiree. I used to 1CC Thunderforce V and Rockman X but now I play word games while drinking tea. You know what? I wouldn't have it any other way. This game is fun, it keeps the brain running, and I gladly paid money for it, and gifted it to one of my private language students, a person in their 20's, whom I see has already played like 4 hours of it. I am a trilingual language-social sciences professor, and have been for like two decades, and sometimes this game beats me anyway, though I have sent back some real words that its dictionary does not seem to have. This is the type of game my 90 year old mother would enjoy on her mobile, but also the type of thing I would prescribe to high schoolers learning ESL. Maybe port it to the Megadrive or Saturn., for twice the pleasure.

I love the idea of combining Balatro's gameplay with other genres, but I'll echo some of the other negative reviews in saying that Word Play has a bunch of severe design flaws which make that combination not particularly fruitful. Including weak jokers, a rather sterile presentation, and most fundamentally, placing far too much of the difficulty in the player's ability to form long words. On higher difficulty levels my gameplay experience eventually turned into typing the letter tiles from my game board into word search websites to find the longest words I could spell with those, and at that point I figured the design was fundamentally untenable. Recommended only if you're a native speaker, have a ridiculously broad vocabulary, and want mostly Boggle with only a dash of Balatro. For us mortals, however, I recommend [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/3856460/Cursed_Words_The_Word_Game_That_Isnt/]Cursed Words: The Word Game That Isn't[/url] instead: a game with pretty much the same premise as Word Play, except that it fixes pretty much every design flaw in the latter game: e.g. you have no letter bag but instead a mechanic which ensures that some special tiles are always in play; jokers are way more powerful and run-defining; there are lots of ways to get wildcards into your game to reduce the need for a huge vocabulary; and so on.

I like the concept, it just plays out a bit boring. Instead of looking like an early mobile game I wish the animations were more impactful and stimulating. I find myself not caring about a next run or if I finish a round at all. Worse than just being boring, the game actively frustrated me. The dictionary is very limited, words like "inhabitance" are not registered as words. I understand that you have the option to petition for words to be added, but the game isn't in early access and there are tons of free resources to get access to all of english words (and their forms) online. The wildcard function also frequently does not work well at all. Almost every time I attempted to use a wildcard tile, the word would not register, even if I was able to make that same word with standard tiles. I would not purchase this unless it is 80% or more off.
